def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    loads = np.zeros_like(bins)
    # Calculate the remaining capacity of each bin
    remaining_capacity = bins - loads
    # Avoid division by zero and ensure bins can fit the item
    valid_bins = remaining_capacity >= item
    # Assign very high priority (low score) to bins that can't fit the item
    priorities = np.full(bins.shape, np.inf)
    # For bins that can fit the item, prioritize based on remaining capacity ratio
    feasible_mask = valid_bins
    if np.any(feasible_mask):
        # Use remaining capacity as a measure of how tightly packed the bin is
        # Lower remaining capacity means higher priority (we want to fill bins efficiently)
        priorities[feasible_mask] = remaining_capacity[feasible_mask]
        # Normalize by bin capacity to account for different bin sizes
        priorities[feasible_mask] /= bins[feasible_mask]
        # Invert so smaller values (more efficient use) have higher priority
        priorities[feasible_mask] = 1 / (priorities[feasible_mask] + 1e-8)
    return priorities

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    loads = np.zeros_like(bins)
    remaining = bins - loads
    feasible_mask = remaining >= item
    priorities = np.full(bins.shape, np.inf)

    if np.any(feasible_mask):
        # Compute current utilization ratio (load / capacity)
        utilization = loads / bins
        # Adjust for item inclusion: expected new utilization if added
        expected_utilization = (loads + item) / bins
        # Measure how close each bin is to an ideal utilization threshold (e.g., 0.75)
        ideal_target = 0.75
        deviation_from_ideal = np.abs(expected_utilization[feasible_mask] - ideal_target)
        # Penalize bins far from ideal utilization
        utilization_penalty = deviation_from_ideal
        # Also penalize bins with very high or very low current load
        load_balance_score = np.where(
            (expected_utilization[feasible_mask] < 0.3) | (expected_utilization[feasible_mask] > 0.9),
            1.0,
            0.0
        )
        # Combine scores: lower is better
        combined_score = utilization_penalty + load_balance_score
        # Invert to prioritize lower scores (higher priority)
        priorities[feasible_mask] = 1 / (combined_score + 1e-8)
    return priorities

    Args:

    """

    # Compute current utilization ratio
    utilization = loads / (bins + 1e-12)
    # Compute remaining capacity
    remaining = bins - item
    # Ensure non-negative remaining capacity
    remaining = np.maximum(remaining, 0)
    # Only consider bins that can fit the item
    can_fit = remaining > 0
    # Initialize priorities with high values (low priority) for bins that can't fit
    priorities = np.full(bins.shape, np.inf)
    # For bins that can fit the item, use log-scaled underutilization
    feasible_mask = can_fit
    if np.any(feasible_mask):
        # Use inverse of utilization to favor less filled bins
        # Apply log transformation to amplify differences in low utilization
        underutilization = 1 - utilization[feasible_mask]
        # Avoid log(0) by small epsilon
        log_underutilization = np.log(1 + underutilization)
        # Normalize and invert so higher values (more underutilized) have higher priority
        priorities[feasible_mask] = log_underutilization / (bins[feasible_mask] + 1e-12)
        # Invert score to make higher priority values better
        priorities[feasible_mask] = 1 / (priorities[feasible_mask] + 1e-8)
    return priorities
